fact: Connecting Africa reports the N'Djamena-Mberé fibre route to the Cameroonian border is currently Chad's only entry point for international capacity from submarine cables, which all land in Cameroon; a revised Sotel-Airtel MoU (suspended by ARCEP) is still needed before the route is adopted.
Chad's telecoms minister said at the Seoul summit that Chad has only one active international internet access, via Cameroon.
Chad told ITU-D that a 35 km fibre link to Cameroon, interconnected with the CAMTEL network and the SAT3 cable, is the only operational link connecting the country to the Internet.

Digital Business Africa reports ARCEP Tchad's director general said in May 2025 that Chad already has gateways with Cameroon and Sudan, depends heavily on neighbours for global internet access, and that one physical cut can interrupt service totally for days.
system: International gateways via Cameroon and Sudan

fact: Sika Finance says Chad has depended on Cameroon's digital infrastructure for 90% of its connectivity since 2015, its only other international route having been put out of service by the war in Sudan.
